 Stanley Tucci to emcee Sundance fundraiser, awards ceremony at Limelight in Boulder 
 Honors to be awarded to Jesse Eisenberg, Gina Prince-Bythewood, Beth de Araújo, Dawn Porter

 By Elizabeth Pond | epond@prairiemountainmedia.com PUBLISHED: November 13, 2026 at 3:01 PM MST | UPDATED: November 13, 2026 at 4:53 PM MST Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... Top L–R: Beth de Araújo, Gine Prince-Bythewood. Bottom L–R: Dawn Porter, Jesse Eisenberg, will all be honored with awards at the the Sundance Film Festival’s annual fundraiser, Celebrating Sundance Institute: The Boulder Debut, at the Limelight Boulder hotel in late January, emceed by Stanley Tucci. (Courtesy of the Sundance Institute) 
 Academy Award–nominated, Emmy- and Golden Globe–winning actor, writer, director, and producer Stanley Tucci will be emceeing the Sundance Film Festival’s annual fundraiser, “Celebrating Sundance Institute: The Boulder Debut,” at the Limelight Boulder hotel in late January, where a range of well-known names will be receiving various filmmaking awards, the Sundance Institute announced in a Friday news release.
 “I am very honored to host,” Tucci said in the release.
 “Sundance Film Festival has played a significant role in my career for close to 40 years, and I am very happy it has found a new home in Boulder so that it might continue to champion independent film.”
 At the Jan. 22 event, Jesse Eisenberg will be honored with the Trailblazer Award, Gina Prince-Bythewood with the Robert Redford Luminary Award, Beth de Araújo with the Vanguard Award for fiction, and Dawn Porter with the Vanguard Award for nonfiction, the release said.
 “We are deeply honored to recognize the incredible and groundbreaking honorees,” said David Linde, CEO of Sundance Institute.
 “This year’s event will be a memorable kickoff to mark a historic first Festival in our new home, while continuing Sundance Institute’s legacy of supporting and honoring bold voices in independent cinema.”
 The influential names of Eisenberg, Araújo, Porter and Prince-Bythewood will likely ring bells for many casual viewers as well as diehard filmmaking enthusiasts.
 Eisenberg, who has long participated in the Sundance Film Festival as an actor in “The Squid and the Whale” (2005), “Holy Rollers” (2010) and “The Double” (2014), and as a filmmaker for “When You Finish Saving the World” (2022) and the Waldo Salt Screenwriting Award-winning “A Real Pain” (2024), will be taking home an honor previously bestowed upon film icons like Christopher Nolan , Chloé Zhao and James Mangold. Eisenberg is also known for his roles in popular films like “The Social Network” (2010), where he played Facebook creator Mark Zuckerberg, and the “Now You See Me” films, where he played the ostensible Four Horsemen illusionist leader Danny Atlas.
 The Trailblazer Award “recognizes an artist’s unwavering dedication and notable contributions to the field of independent film,” the release said.
 Eisenberg has also released a new film this year, “The Debut,” starring Julianne Moore and Paul Giamatti.
 “Every time I’ve been invited to the Sundance Film Festival, I’ve jumped for joy,” Eisenberg said in the release. “This time, I’m jumping with joy and gratitude. I’m so honored — and surprised — to receive the Trailblazer Award.”
 Prince-Bythewood is known, among other things, for her debut feature “Love & Basketball,” which premiered at the 2000 Sundance Film Festival, along with her 2017 episodic series “Shots Fired,” which was co-created with her partner Reggie Rock Bythewood.
 Prince-Bythewood has also contributed to the festival through her involvement in developing the 1998 January Screenwriters Lab, 1998 Directors Lab, 1998 Screenplay Reading Series, and the 1998 June Screenwriters Lab, and through her service as a creative advisor for the 2023 Directors Lab.
 The Robert Redford Luminary Award, the honor that will be given to Prince-Bythewood, was a new addition to Sundance’s programming in January 2026. It was added to the award lineup following the passing of film icon Redford, who died in September 2025 at 89 years old.
 The award “recognizes and celebrates individuals who have, in a visionary way, used their resources, insights, and reach to create possibility where there wasn’t, thus doing their part to make the world a better place,” the release said.
 The honor was previously given to Ed Harris and Gyula Gazdag.
 “The Sundance Institute labs changed the trajectory of my life,” Prince-Bythewood said in the release. “Every single studio and production company passed on ‘Love & Basketball.’ And then the labs called to invite me and the script to be a part of their world. I am forever grateful for Robert Redford’s vision to amplify the silenced voices, to champion the untold stories, and to believe in first-time filmmakers. Receiving this award that honors him is incredibly meaningful and feels beautifully full circle.”
 Beth de Araújo is best known for her second feature, “Josephine” (2026), which was supported by the Feature Film Program labs and won the U.S. Grand Jury Prize for drama and the  Audience Award for drama at the 2026 Sundance Film Festival. The film was acquired by Sumerian Pictures for a theatrical release in the fall. She was also nominated for the 2022 Gotham Award for Breakthrough Director for her debut film, “Soft & Quiet,” which premiered at SXSW in 2022.
“The Sundance Institute community has built and fostered a home for countless artists, one that encourages us to share our stories with uncompromising vision,” Araújo said in the release. “Without this support, I could not have started this career. I am so excited to see the Festival and the Institute programs that I hold so dear thrive and grow in Boulder.”
 The Vanguard Awards “honor emerging artists whose work highlights the art of storytelling and creative independence in both fiction and nonfiction,” the release said. Araújo will be given the Vanguard Award for Fiction, and Porter for nonfiction.
 Porter is known for her award-winning documentary filmmaking, including “When A Witness Recants” (2026), her founding of Trilogy Films and her four-time Sundance Film Festival directorial work.
 Porter, who was awarded the National Humanities Medal in 2024 by former President Joe Biden at the White House, has had her work appear on HBO, Netflix, ESPN, PBS, Hulu, Apple TV and Showtime.
 “Sundance Institute has been such a critical partner in my career path,” Porter said in the release. “From the documentary labs to festival premieres and so much more, my career would not be what it is without Sundance Institute. It is truly an honor to mark this new chapter.”
 Previous recipients of the fiction and nonfiction Vanguard Awards include Nia DaCosta; Geeta Gandbhir; Sean Wang; Julian Brave NoiseCat; Emily Kassie; Celine Song; Maite Alberdi; Ryan Coogler; W. Kamau Bell; Nikyatu Jusu; Siân Heder; Ahmir “Questlove” Thompson; Radha Blank; Lulu Wang; Boots Riley; Dee Rees; Marielle Heller; Damien Chazelle and Benh Zeitlin, among others.
 The annual gala is used by the institute as a way to honor impactful individuals and fundraise for the nonprofit.
“This special evening directly supports the Institute’s core mission to nurture and uplift independent storytellers around the world through our labs, grants, and public programs. We look forward to welcoming our community to celebrate our extraordinary honorees and champion the values that continue to guide us,” Ebs Burnough, Sundance Institute Board Chair, said in the release.
 Sundance will be venturing out of its long-term home of Park City, Utah and coming to Boulder for the first time from Jan. 21-31.
 “We are thrilled to come together for the first time in Boulder for our annual gathering,” said Michelle Satter, founding senior director of artist programs at Sundance Institute, in the release.
